name: Meridian Standard Chrome-Last Boot
description:
A no-nonsense, wide-last work boot manufactured to fit the most common prosthetic foot models on the market. The sizing system uses prosthetic model codes rather than conventional shoe sizes — you order by your chrome model number, not your old biological size. Leather upper, steel shank, thick rubber sole. It looks like a plain work boot and functions like one.

Mass-produced and stocked at every Tier 2 hardware and supply depot in GLMZ. The boot of choice for augmented workers who just need something that fits and lasts. Zero fashion intent, complete functional reliability.
functionality: Manufactured to fit standard prosthetic foot model codes. Wide last accommodates most common chrome foot profiles without modification.
what_it_says: You don't have time for fashion. You have a job, you have chrome, you need boots that fit.
worn_by: Tier 2 laborers with standard prosthetic feet
story_hooks: Because they're ordered by prosthetic model code, a pair of Meridian Standards tells you exactly what chrome someone is running — useful or dangerous information depending on context.
An underground modification scene has sprung up around these boots — people customizing the plain shells into something personal.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian work boot with a distinctly widened last designed for prosthetic foot integration. Heavy, purposeful silhouette that sits flat and stable. No aesthetic flourish—pure industrial form following function. The boot reads as infrastructure rather than fashion.
physical_description.fit: Wide, roomy last accommodating prosthetic feet and cybernetic ankles. Structured around chrome foot geometry rather than biological anatomy. The fit is deliberately generous to allow mounting hardware and articulation systems without compression.
physical_description.primary_material: Scuffed treated leather upper (tan or dark brown) with visible grain marks from industrial tanning. Reinforced stitching throughout. Steel shank embedded in sole structure visible at heel.
physical_description.texture: Rough, work-worn leather with tool marks and creasing. Sole is thick vulcanized rubber with aggressive tread pattern. Metal eyelets and heel plate catch light. Overall tactile impression is heavy and durable.
physical_description.color_scheme: Muted earth tones—tan, chocolate brown, or weathered grey. Chrome hardware (heel plate, eyelets, shank reinforcement) provides metallic accents. No branding beyond small stamped model codes on the tongue and heel.
physical_description.closures: Traditional lace-up with metal eyelets and secondary locking mechanism—speed-lace option with friction-fit toggle at midfoot for quick adjustments with gloved or augmented hands.
distinctive_features: Prosthetic model code sizing (not human shoe sizes) marked on tongue and insole
Recessed mounting points on sole for modular foot attachment systems
Reinforced heel counter with steel plate for prosthetic socket stability
Rocker-geometry sole designed for servo-motor gait compensation
Drain holes near toe box for water management in augmented feet
Serial number embossed on leather for supply chain tracking
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3—functional working class. Produced at industrial scale, affordable, ubiquitous in labor zones. No luxury markers, no customization tax.
physical_description.cultural_context: The boot of augmented laborers, warehouse workers, maintenance crews, anyone with chrome limbs who needs dependable footwear. Signals honest work and visible augmentation acceptance. Wearing this means your prosthetics are open-source or standardized, not bespoke corpo hardware.
physical_description.condition_typical: Weathered and broken-in. Scuffs, mud stains, oil marks. Laces replaced multiple times. Insole may show compression. Sole edges worn darker from repetitive contact. Still structurally sound—these boots are meant to outlast the feet they hold.
